```{r, include=FALSE}
library(circular)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

### General Notes:

$\mu_i = 2\arctan(\beta_0 + X_i^T\beta)$ : link function

$Y_i \mid X_i \sim \mathrm{VM}(\mu_i, \kappa)$ : Von Meises distribution

Concentration Parameter $\kappa$:

0 - uniform dist around circle

0.5 - very low concentration

1 - low concentration

5 - moderate concentration

10 - high concentration

20 - very high concentration

### Model (10/30)

```{r}
set.seed(1)

# predictors
n <- 5000
x <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n), x3 = rnorm(n))

# parameters
k <- 5 
beta <- c(0,0.5, 0.5) #starting simple
beta0 <- 2

# calculating linear predictors and conditional mean directions
xb <- as.vector(as.matrix(x) %*% beta)

# link function -> mu = 2arctan(xbeta), when we run it through this, we are getting back to the angles
mu <- beta0 + 2 * atan(xb) 

# generate circular responses from VM dist
y <- sapply(mu, function(m) {
  as.numeric(rvonmises(1, mu = circular(m), kappa = k))
})

# visualizing simulated responses using rose diagram
rose.diag(circular(y), bins = 24, col = "mediumvioletred")

# creating simulated dataset
sim_data <- data.frame(x, y)
#head(sim_data)

# linear regression
mod1 <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = sim_data)
summary(mod1)

# circular regression
mod2 <- lm.circular(y = circular(y), x = as.matrix(x), type = "c-l", init = c(0, 0, 0))

```

We want to answer the question: How does kappa (concentration) and the location of the splitting point affect the accuracy of linear regression when analyzing circular data, and under what conditions is circular regression necessary?

\^ doing this by looking at the $\mu$s

\^ by rotating the responses, we are changing the splitting point.

### Simulating with different values of Kappa (11/06)

### Rotation = 0 (standard)

```{r}
set.seed(1)

# parameters
n <- 500
beta0 <- 2
beta <- 2

# vary kappas
kappas <- c(0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1)

# different rotations
rotation <- 0

# store estimates
beta_linear_0 <- beta_circular_0 <- list()

nsim <- 100

for (i in 1:length(kappas)) {
  
  k <- kappas[i]
  beta_linear_0[[i]] <- beta_circular_0[[i]] <- list()
  
  for (j in 1:nsim) {
    print(j)
    
    x <- rnorm(n)
    mu <- beta0 + 2*atan(beta*x)
    
    # generate original circular responses
    y_original <- sapply(mu, function(m) {
      as.numeric(rvonmises(1, mu = circular(m), kappa = k))})
    
    # rotate observations and split at 0
    y <- (y_original - rotation) %% (2*pi)
    
    # fit linear regression
    mod1 <- lm(y ~ x)
    
    beta_linear_0[[i]][j] <- coef(mod1)[1] + mean(x) * coef(mod1)[2]
    
    # fit circular regression
    mod2 <- lm.circular(y = circular(y), x = matrix(x, ncol = 1), type = "c-l", init = 1)
    
    beta_circular_0[[i]][j] <- mod2$mu + 2*atan(mean(x) * mod2$coefficients[1])
  }
}

data.frame(beta_circ = unlist(lapply(beta_circular_0, function(x){mean(unlist(x))})), beta_linear = unlist(lapply(beta_linear_0, function(x){mean(unlist(x))})), kappa = kappas) 

results_0 <- data.frame(beta =  c(unlist(lapply(beta_circular_0, function(x){mean(unlist(x))})),unlist(lapply(beta_linear_0, function(x){mean(unlist(x))}))), type = c(rep("circ",length(kappas)),rep("linear",length(kappas))), kappa = rep(kappas,2))

results_0 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = kappa, y = beta, color = type )) + 
  geom_line()

rose.diag(y, bins = 24, main = paste("Y, kappa =", k))
rose.diag(x, bins = 24, main = paste("X, kappa =", k))

plot(x,y)

unlist(lapply(beta_circular_0, function(x){sd(unlist(x))}))

# results
results_0 <- data.frame(kappa = kappas, beta_linear = unlist(lapply(beta_linear_0, function(x) { mean(unlist(x), na.rm = TRUE)})), beta_circular = unlist(lapply(beta_circular_0, function(x) { mean(unlist(x), na.rm = TRUE)})))
results_0

data.frame(x = x,y =y, r = 1)  %>% ggplot(aes(x = y, y = r, color = x)) + geom_point() + coord_polar() + scale_color_viridis_b()
```

### 4 results plotted next to each other

different splits with kappas on the x-axis

```{r}

# combine results from all four rotations
results_all <- rbind(
  data.frame(results_0, rotation = "0"),
  data.frame(results_45, rotation = "pi/4"),
  data.frame(results_90, rotation = "pi/2"),
  data.frame(results_180, rotation = "pi"))

results_long <- results_all %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(beta_linear, beta_circular),names_to = "method",values_to = "estimate")

# order rotations
results_long$rotation <- factor(results_long$rotation, levels = c("0", "pi/4", "pi/2", "pi"))

# plot
ggplot(results_long,
       aes(x = kappa, y = estimate, color = method)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ rotation, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual( values = c("beta_linear" = "deeppink", "beta_circular" = "deepskyblue"), labels = c("Linear", "Circular")) + labs( title = "Different Rotations: Linear vs Circular Reg", x = "Kappa", y = "Estimated Mean Response", color = "Regression Method") + theme_minimal()

```

when we split at 0, the estimated mean responses for linear and circular regression are similar. As we rotate the split, the difference between the mean responses for each method gets bigger. (linear and circular reg are producing diff results.
